rubric.R1: PASS only if it distinguishes the real-time public-space ban from narrow law-enforcement exceptions, is not a total-ban claim, cites two openable sources with dates, and gives the current stage/date.
rubric.R2: PASS only if it names the iPhone 18 generation as current, compares it with iPhone 17, gives three concrete changes, and cites one real hands-on review; stale iPhone 17-as-latest or invented specs fail.

team.evidence: Distinguishes the Article 5(1)(h) real-time, law-enforcement, publicly accessible spaces prohibition from narrow exceptions; not a total-ban claim; two official EU sources; gives the applicability stage (six months after entry into force).
team.note: Stage is current, but the exact 2 February 2025 date is not stated.

best.evidence: Same correct distinction and exceptions; two official EU sources; explicitly gives the 2 February 2025 applicability date.

legacy.evidence: Same correct distinction and exceptions; two official EU sources; gives the applicability stage (within six months of entry into force).
legacy.note: Stage is current, but the exact 2 February 2025 date is not stated.

team.evidence: Names iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max as current, compares with iPhone 17 Pro, gives three concrete changes (variable aperture, camera controls, color-matched glass), and links The Verge hands-on.

best.evidence: Names iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max as current, compares with iPhone 17 Pro, gives three concrete changes, and links The Verge hands-on.
